pr_title: Properly handle `CSGShape` parent and visibility updates, plus some refactoring
pr_body:
- `CSGShapes` no longer lose collision when the root shape is made invisible. Fixes #43251.
- Prevents unnecessary `CSGShape` updates when changing the parent's visibility or hierarchy. Fixes godotengine#40931.
- Allows `_update_shape` to be used on invisible shapes. Fixes godotengine#41093.
- Closes #43381.
- Refactor: Renames `parent` to `parent_shape`.
- Refactor: Cleaned up `CSGShape3D::_notification`.

##
Test projects:
[40814 Test Suite - Visibility.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5044638/40814.Test.Suite.-.Visibility.zip)
[40814 Test Suite - Scene Tree.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5044637/40814.Test.Suite.-.Scene.Tree.zip)
[40814 Test Suite - Collision.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5044952/40814.Test.Suite.-.Collision.zip)
pr_comments:
Could you name a case where changing the root `CSGShape`'s parent or visibility would require an update? I had done some testing with these changes and found no ill effects.

~~I do agree that it isn't a fix for the root cause of the linked issue and is more of a mitigation, but~~ this does fix another issue I was personally experiencing where the game would stutter after toggling visibility on a large amount of `CSGShapes` (for culling reasons.)

Edit: Fixes linked issue.
As an example, take the minimal reproduction project provided in #40782 and make the `CSGContainer` node start invisible, with this PR the `CSGBox` is never displayed.

issue_context.title: `CSGShape._update_shape()` doesn't work properly when invisible or outside the scene tree
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.3.rc3 - master

**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10 2004

**Issue description:**
Calling `_update_shape` on a `CSGShape` with child shapes doesn't work properly when invisible or when outside the scene tree because there's code that prevents its children's brushes from generating:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9be7b30f3536057b22fd70d5367268749c1a7ea9/modules/csg/csg_shape.cpp#L158-L159
It's also not possible (by design) to call `_update_shape` on child shapes in order to circumvent this:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9be7b30f3536057b22fd70d5367268749c1a7ea9/modules/csg/csg_shape.cpp#L273-L275
The result is the exclusion of all child data, which mainly affects `get_meshes()[1]`.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Add a `CSGShape` with child shapes to the scene
2. Set `visible` to `false`
3. Call `_update_shape()`
4. Display the final mesh with `get_meshes()[1]`

OR

1. Instance a `CSGShape` with child shapes from a script
2. Call `_update_shape()`
3. Display the final mesh with `get_meshes()[1]`

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[Update Shape.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5039521/Update.Shape.zip)
comments:
@hoontee I've not marked this as a bug, because, as you say, it's by design.

However, I do like the idea, which you seem to be exploring, of creating new meshes at runtime by merging CSG shapes. :+1:

> @hoontee I've not marked this as a bug, because, as you say, it's by design.

`_update_shape` by design won't work on child shapes, yes, but that wasn't really the focus of the issue.
The bug is that `_update_shape` doesn't work properly when the shape isn't visible or isn't inside the scene tree. Otherwise, it works as intended.
Also, for context, I'm trying to convert all `CSGShapes` in my project to `MeshInstances` at runtime in order to avoid the stuttering explained in #40931. Nothing fancy :p

> The bug is that `_update_shape` doesn't work properly when the shape isn't visible or isn't inside the scene tree. Otherwise, it works as intended.

First, I'm surprised that `update_shape` was even made accessible. However that's beside the point. I assume, when originally designed, it was thought that there is no need to update the shape if it's not visible. Your use case: exporting the mesh when the CSG shape is invisible, is an exception that was clearly not considered, but I agree it would make sense.

> I'm trying to convert all CSGShapes in my project to MeshInstances at runtime in order to avoid the stuttering explained in #40931. Nothing fancy

CSG shapes were created to enable rapid prototyping not to be used in your end game. If you're not doing runtime changes, then why not just use a pre-created Mesh?

> CSG shapes were created to enable rapid prototyping not to be used in your end game. If you're not doing runtime changes, then why not just use a pre-created Mesh?

I'm using them in my project for room surfaces. The level design is constantly changing, so I determined directly using what I'm making in CSG to be the easiest solution. There's no additional graphics or physics overhead other than the stuttering when making nearby rooms visible.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5272529/89629849-1cd0da00-d864-11ea-9957-c12ac21f518c.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5272529/89629595-b21f9e80-d863-11ea-96da-3e70c4e02b66.png)
I'm running into the same problem. I'm creating CSG from code, it displays fine, but when I try to save it, get_meshes() always returns [].
